purpose: Amlodipine is used to treat high blood pressure and chest pain called angina. Lowering high blood pressure helps prevent strokes, heart attacks, and kidney problems. It can also help you exercise more without getting chest pain.
how_it_works: Your heart and blood vessels have tiny channels that let calcium in, which causes them to squeeze tightly. Amlodipine blocks those calcium channels, so your blood vessels relax and widen. This makes it easier for your heart to pump blood and lowers your blood pressure.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are swelling in your ankles or feet, feeling flushed or warm in your face, headache, and dizziness. Some people feel more tired than usual or have an upset stomach. These effects are usually mild and often get better after the first few weeks.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have liver problems, since this medicine stays in your body longer and may need a lower dose. Do not suddenly stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor, especially if you have chest pain. Let your doctor know if swelling gets severe or if you feel very dizzy or faint, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
typical_dosing: Most adults start with 5 mg taken by mouth once a day, usually at the same time each day. Your doctor may increase your dose to 10 mg once daily if needed. You can take it with or without food, and it works best when taken consistently every day.
